A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TacFiLM research work. All pages, figures, tables and equations support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original real-robot insertion experiments, robustness tests, FiLM ablations and tactile-encoder classification results in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original empirical results and adds drawer-opening experiments, cross-attention comparisons and tactile force-regression results.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 substantially revises the stated action-generation procedure: v1 describes autoregressive prediction of discrete action tokens, whereas v2 describes an MLP action head using L1 regression to predict continuous action chunks. The FiLM fusion mechanism remains unchanged. This establishes a change in the reported model, without establishing that the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds drawer opening, extending robot evaluation beyond insertion to hooking and pulling. It also adds continuous force estimation from Sparsh TacBench to the encoder evaluation. The original insertion tasks, camera-degradation scenarios and three classification tasks remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds Cross-Attn alongside OpenVLA-OFT and TactileConcat throughout the main comparisons and camera-robustness tests in Tables 1–2. This is an implemented fusion baseline following PolyTouch, using six residual cross-attention blocks on the shared OpenVLA-OFT backbone, rather than merely an additional citation.

E3.justification: V2 extends success and direct-completion criteria to drawer opening and introduces RMSE evaluation for continuous force estimation. The stated 80k training steps and 30 ID/15 OOD rollouts per task-method remain unchanged. Increased aggregate rollout counts accompany the expanded tasks and comparisons.

E4.justification: Table 2 extends the existing camera-degradation tests to Cross-Attn, reporting 53.33% success under dimming and 46.67% with reduced frame updates. Figure 5 also adds its force and completion-time profiles. The FiLM-depth ablation and the existing perturbation conditions are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same per-condition rollout counts and force/time mean-plus-minus reporting, shaded force curves and completion-time boxplots. V2 introduces no new seed information, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures. Additional comparison rows do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive Cross-Attn results, drawer-opening results and force-estimation scores. Drawer success is 86.67% for TacFiLM, versus 33.33% for OpenVLA-OFT, 26.67% for TactileConcat and 20.00% for Cross-Attn. Table 3 adds force RMSE of 36.09 for Sparsh-DINO versus 58.64 for T3. Existing task-level numerical results are retained; revised ID averages cover an expanded task mix.

T1.justification: Equation (1) retains the same affine FiLM transformation. V2 introduces explicit time/block indices and aligns the diagram notation, without changing the mathematical operation. Neither version presents formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central lightweight tactile-fusion contribution remains. V2 extends the abstract to drawer opening and the contribution/conclusion comparisons to cross-attention. The introduction changes the claimed ID improvement from up to 30% to up to 50%, while revising the claimed HDMI advantage from 50% to 30%.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds the hypothesis that cross-attention underperforms because its additional trainable multimodal interactions require more task-specific data. Section 4.3 interprets its camera-condition results as poor robustness. The limitations concerning task diversity and extension to other VLA backbones remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies that LoRA targets both OpenVLA-OFT and tactile-backbone linear layers, with FiLM layers trained from scratch. It supplies insertion/drawer language prompts and Cross-Attn implementation details, and adds a project-page link. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish code or data availability.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same 73 works. Section 2.2 adds a focused comparison of concatenation and cross-attention, positioning TacFiLM against increased token length and additional attention parameters. The new baseline is explicitly related to PolyTouch.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording, terminology and affiliation edits, rewrites the action-generation paragraph, and expands related-work and experimental explanations. The section sequence and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 5 add Cross-Attn; Figure 3 adds drawer opening and ID/OOD grouping; Figure 4 replaces the circle-peg rollout with a drawer rollout. Tables 1–3 gain rows and grouping labels. These extend the existing displays while largely retaining their organization and the document's layout.

improvement.justification: The shared-backbone cross-attention comparison and drawer-opening task strengthen evidence for the fusion choice and applicability beyond insertion; added implementation details also help reproducibility. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: v2 Table 1 gives OpenVLA-OFT an ID average of 58.10%, although its four task rates imply 55.00% under the stated equal rollout counts. Section 4.3 also retains a lowest-force claim despite Table 2 showing Cross-Attn at 7.53 N versus TacFiLM at 8.12 N under reduced frame updates.
